### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 each occurred exactly once in every trace (participation 100%, about 1 occurrence per trace, no repetition). In the later window they still occur in every trace but average about 3 occurrences per trace, and about 67–68 in 100 traces contain repeats of each of them. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- The routing out of A38 changed: before, about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A25; after, about 67 in 100 go to A30 and about 33 in 100 to A25, with small new edges to A04, A02 and A27. [DIR001]
- Pairwise order among these five activities changed from fixed or mixed single-pass orders to mostly interleaved-or-repeated: A30 preceded A31/A36/A37/A38 in all or nearly all traces before versus about 32–34 in 100 after, with interleaved-or-repeated rising from 0 to about 66–68 in 100; pairs such as A31/A36 and A36/A37, previously split roughly 50/50 between both orders, now show interleaving or repetition in about 66 in 100 traces. The five activities still co-occur in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Gaps between consecutive occurrences widened: for pairs such as A31→A36, a gap of 1 step fell from about 66 in 100 to about 12 in 100, and gaps of 3–5 steps appeared; A37→A37 repetition, seen in only 1 trace before, appears in 109 traces after with gaps of 3–5 steps. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]
- The position distributions of the five activities roughly doubled in spread (for example A30's standard deviation rose from about 0.05 to about 0.14) with slightly later mean positions, consistent with multiple occurrences per trace rather than a move of a single occurrence. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- A04, a rare activity, appeared in about 9 of 200 traces before versus about 29 of 200 after (participation about 4.5% to about 14.5%). [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the group of activities A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38, previously executed exactly once per trace in a fixed sequence ending at A38, is now repeated within traces — about three passes per trace in roughly two-thirds of cases — with A38 passing back to A30 in about two-thirds of its outgoing transitions instead of proceeding to A25. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR001]

The supporting signs are direct and consistent: repetition of each activity is observed directly (recurrence support rising from 0 to about 0.67 with unchanged 100% participation), the successor change at A38 is observed directly, and all ten activity pairs show the same interleaved-or-repeated share (about 0.66–0.68) that matches the recurrence rates, together with wider gaps between occurrences. With 29 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance in the control-flow family, chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [OCC002, OCC006, DIR001, REL001, REL010, LAG001, LAG007]

Limitations: the full repeated path is not traced step by step (no relational or lag items cover A30's outgoing side), so whether all five activities repeat together as one block in each cycle is inferred from the matching rates rather than observed directly; the relation indicator also cannot separate interleaving from repetition, although the occurrence counts confirm that repetition itself occurs. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that the five activities run concurrently in the later window, which would also produce interleaving — though the observed back-edge from A38 to A30 favours the sequential-loop reading. [REL001, REL005, DIR001, OCC002]

Other differences: A04 became more frequent (about 9 versus 29 of 200 traces) and A38 gained a small direct edge to A04; both rest on few observations and are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC001, DIR001]
